R/o.19-4-7/A/157, AL-Jubair Colony, Falaknnuma, Chandrayangutta, Hyderabad now detained in Special Prison for woman Chanchalguda, Hyderabad before this Honourable Court and she may be ordered to be released forthwith or/set at liberty after declaring her detention order vide proceedings No. 154/PD CCRB/RCKD/2021 dated 08.12.2021 passed by the 2nd respondent as illegal, unconstitutional, arbitrary and violation of Article 14 and 21 of the Constitution of India and violation of Principles of natural justice and
pass such other order...

" 
2. This writ petition is filed by the son of detenue- Smt.Raziya Sulthana @ Harshiya challenging the order of detention dated 08.12.2021 made under Section 3 (2) of the Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders,
Land-Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertilizer Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Documents Offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders,
Cyber Crime offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (Amendment Act No. 13 of 2018).
3. Heard Sri L.K. Sharma, learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Government Pleader for Home representing learned Additional Advocate General appearing for the respondents.
4. Cr.No.453 of 2021 was registered on 5.11.2021 in Balanagar Police Station, under Sections 366-A,
370-A of Indian Penal Code, Section 8 of The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (for short 'the POSCO Act') and Sections 3, 4, 5 and 7 of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act 1956.

sentences.text: The detenue was arrested on 5.11.2021.
Consequent to bail granted by the competent Court, she was released on 7.12.2021.
Having come to know of the bail granted to the detenue, the order of detention was made on 08.12.2021 and detenue was taken into custody on 15.12.2021.

5. A reading of the detention order would go to show that detaining authority has taken an extreme measure of preventively detaining the detenue on the ground that she is involved in heinous crime of immoral trafficking of woman particularly minor and that conduct of the detenue being grave, if she is allowed to go scot-free, there is possibility of detenue indulging in committing similar crimes,
thereby offending the public order.
6.

From a reading of the detention order and also from the counter affidavit, it is apparent that there is no criminal background and involvement of the detenue in similar crimes or in any other type of crimes previously and this appears to be solitary incident.
7. Further learned counsel for the petitioner submits that detenue has two young daughters to take care of and because of her detention, no personal attention could be paid to her daughters.

He would submit that while granting bail, the Fast Track Special Sessions Judge for Trial and Disposal of Cases under POSCO Act, Ranga Reddy District, has imposed stringent conditions and therefore,
there is no justification to resort to extreme measure of detaining the detenue.

sentences.text: In the order granting bail on 06.11.2021, the Special Sessions Judge, directed the detenue to execute personal bond for Rs.25,000/- with two sureties each for a like sum; to appear before the concerned Station House Officer on every Sunday between 10.30 A.M. to 12.00 noon for a period of 60 days or till filing of charge sheet, whichever is earlier and should not leave India without previous permission of the Court.
9. Having regard to the facts of this case, it cannot be said that a grave public order is affected and preventive detention of the detenue is required.
What is alleged against the detenue can be prosecuted as a part of enforcement of law and order.
Therefore, the Order of detention is set aside.

However, this order does not come in the way of competent authority exercising his powers, if so warranted, if the detenue continues to indulge in similar crimes.
10.
In the result, the Writ Petition is allowed.

The impugned detention order passed by the Office of t h e C o m m i s s i o n e r o f P o l i c e , R a c h a k o n d a - 2 n d r e s p o n d e n t v i d e N o . 1 5 4 / P D CELL/CCRB/RCKD/2021 dated 08.12.2021 is hereby set aside.
The respondents are directed to set the detenue, namely Smt.Raziya Sulthana @ Harshiya D/o.

Mohammad Osman, W/o.Mohammad Wasim Shareef, Aged 35 yrs, R/o.Flat No.305, Opposite to Osmania Hotel, Shaheennagar, Balapur,
N/o.H.No.19-4-7/A/157, Al-Jubial Colony, Falaknuma, Chandrayanagutta, Hyderabad, Aadhar No.731352289227 at liberty forthwith, if she is no longer required in any other criminal case.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
